questions.q: What is AutoInvoice, functionally, compared to Import Journals or Import Payables Invoices?
options: A completely unrelated tool with no connection to the FBDI pipeline
Receivables' name for the same role: the product-specific import process that validates staged data and creates real records
A manual data-entry screen with no automation
A tool only used for deleting old transactions
questions.explain: AutoInvoice is the Receivables-specific name for the same kind of process as Import Journals or Import Payables Invoices — it reads staged data and creates real transactions.

questions.q: Which interface table does AutoInvoice read staged transaction lines from?
options: GL_INTERFACE
AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE
RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL
FA_MASS_ADDITIONS
questions.explain: RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL is the Receivables transaction-line staging table that AutoInvoice reads from.

questions.q: What is a 'grouping rule' in the context of AutoInvoice?
options: A rule for formatting Excel cell colors
Configured logic that determines which transaction lines belong together on the same invoice, based on shared attributes like customer and date
A rule limiting how many suppliers can exist
A password policy for Oracle Fusion logins
questions.explain: Grouping rules are specific to Receivables/AutoInvoice — they assemble individually staged lines into complete invoices based on shared attributes.

questions.q: Why does AutoInvoice need grouping rules when a Payables invoice does not?
options: Because Receivables transaction lines typically arrive without an explicit header that already groups them, unlike a payables invoice header-and-lines structure
Because Receivables has no interface tables at all
Because grouping rules are purely cosmetic and have no functional purpose
Because Payables invoices never have more than one line
questions.explain: A payables invoice header already explicitly groups its own lines. Receivables lines arrive more loosely, so grouping rules are needed to assemble them into transactions.

questions.q: In the lesson's scenario, two lines fail to combine onto one invoice. What was the likely cause?
options: The UCM account was wrong
One line had a grouping attribute (such as a transaction date) formatted inconsistently with its sibling line, preventing a confident match
Macros were disabled in Excel
The supplier did not exist yet
questions.explain: Grouping depends on shared attributes matching between lines. An inconsistency in one of those attributes can prevent AutoInvoice from grouping the lines as intended.
